text:
Kaapo Kakko will never win a race (his top speed sits in the 5th percentile of the league), and it doesn't seem to matter much. The former second overall pick has 16 points in 21 games for Seattle on about 14 minutes a night, and the Kakko, Matty Beniers and Mackie Samoskevich line "cooked" in last week's 5-1 win over Vancouver, as the Kraken's Alison Lukan put it.

He scores by thinking. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had 19% of his setups last season coming from behind the net, more than double a typical forward, and 67% of his exits leaving the zone with the puck. At 5v5 Seattle is better by four and a half points of expected-goal share with him on the ice than without, even if the team is under 50% overall.

The production is running hot, though. He's shooting 20% on just 25 shots, and Seattle has scored 7.7 more goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice. His points rate (3.2 per 60) is above even the top of the range we'd give him. Evolving-Hockey noted last season that weak linemates hid his value; this year the bounces are doing the opposite.
